The engine and its languages:
import pytesseract as tess
print(tess.get_tesseract_version())
langs = tess.get_languages()
print(len(langs), langs[:5])
print('eng' in langs, 'xyz' in langs)
Reading one line of text:
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import pytesseract as tess
font = ImageFont.load_default(size=40)
im = Image.new('L', (440, 90), 255)
ImageDraw.Draw(im).text((20, 20), 'Hello OCR 2026', fill=0, font=font)
text = tess.image_to_string(im)
print(repr(text))
print(text.strip() == 'Hello OCR 2026')

Telling Tesseract what to expect:
import pytesseract as tess
# im holds the line: Call 555-0199 now: 2026
print(repr(tess.image_to_string(im).strip()))
digits = '--psm 7 -c tessedit_char_whitelist=0123456789-'

Finding the mistakes of a reading:
import difflib
TRUTH = 'Invoice 2026-114 total 482.50'
read = 'lnvoice 2O26-114 totaI 482.5O'
for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, TRUTH, read).get_opcodes():
    if tag != 'equal':
        print(tag, repr(TRUTH[i1:i2]), 'read as', repr(read[j1:j2]))
ratio = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, TRUTH, read).ratio()
print(round(ratio, 2))
A searchable PDF:
import subprocess, tempfile
import pytesseract as tess
# im holds two lines of text
pdf = tess.image_to_pdf_or_hocr(im, extension='pdf')
print(type(pdf).__name__, pdf[:5])
path = tempfile.mktemp(suffix='.pdf')
open(path, 'wb').write(pdf)
done = subprocess.run(['pdftotext', path, '-'], capture_output=True, text=True)
print([t for t in done.stdout.splitlines() if t.strip()])

Practice program: browser text scraper:
def screenshot(n):
    im = Image.new('RGB', (640, 160), 'white')
    line = f'Page {n} of 3: total {n * 100}.50'
    ImageDraw.Draw(im).text((20, 50), line, fill='black', font=font)
    return im
for n in (1, 2, 3):
    part = screenshot(n).crop((0, 20, 640, 120))
    text = tess.image_to_string(part).strip()
    with open('output.txt', 'a') as f:
        f.write(text + '\n')
print(open('output.txt').read().splitlines())
